items.title: HCLTech Builds AI Agents On NVIDIA Omniverse To Test Cars Inside Virtual Worlds
items.summary: HCL Tech is using Nvidia technology to replace physical vehicle testing with virtual simulation environments. Learn how this shift accelerates software validation for modern cars. Modern vehicles are essentially computers on wheels, making traditional manual testing a major bottleneck for software-defined vehicle development. HCL Tech has launched a new validation offering that utilizes the Nvidia Omniverse and Isaac SIM platforms to simulate thousands of safety-critical edge cases, reducing the reliance on dangerous or expensive physical road tests. The system integrates the Nvidia agent toolkit and Neotron open models to automate test creation, compliance reporting, and failure investigation. By automating these processes, the partnership aims to solve the primary constraint currently facing the software-defined vehicle industry. HCL Tech is using Nvidia technology to replace physical vehicle testing with virtual simulation environments. Learn how this shift accelerates software validation for modern cars.

Modern vehicles are essentially computers on wheels, making traditional manual testing a major bottleneck for software-defined vehicle development. HCL Tech has launched a new validation offering that utilizes the Nvidia Omniverse and Isaac SIM platforms to simulate thousands of safety-critical edge cases, reducing the reliance on dangerous or expensive physical road tests.

The system integrates the Nvidia agent toolkit and Neotron open models to automate test creation, compliance reporting, and failure investigation. This transition also raises significant questions regarding legal liability when autonomous AI agents are responsible for safety validation in virtual environments.

items.title: The Trojan Horse in AI-Written Mathematics
items.summary: Kevin Hartnett, author of The Proof in the Code, on the catch in AI autoformalisation. An LLM can now turn a maths paper into Lean code in a fraction of the time a team of humans would take, and the Mathlib community is finding that's a little bit of a Trojan horse: a flood of Lean that isn't written with the precision and economy Mathlib's canonical definitions need. It's the same problem everyone else has with the volume of AI-generated everything. From our documentary "Mathematics Just Changed Forever" with Kevin Hartnett, Kevin Buzzard, Jeremy Avigad, Leo de Moura and Paul Lessard. Watch the full conversation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IRJDwtAreB4

items.title: What is quantum machine learning, really?
items.summary: Artificial intelligence has transformed the way researchers explore some of the world’s biggest problems, but what happens when machine learning meets quantum computing? The topic of quantum machine learning has generated enormous interest in recent years, but fundamental questions remain: What specifically counts as QML? Where might quantum computers deliver computational advantages over classical AI? What would a convincing demonstration of that advantage actually look like? In this episode of The Coherence Times, we sit down with IBM Research’s Kunal Sharma and EPFL’s Zoe Holmes to explore the rapidly evolving field of quantum machine learning. Together, they discuss the complex relationship between quantum computing and AI, how AI can help improve quantum algorithms, and what it will take for quantum machine learning to move from theory to practical applications. The opinions expressed in this podcast are solely those of the participants and do not necessarily reflect the views of IBM or any other organization or entity. Want to learn more about quantum computing and quantum machine learning? Head to the Learning page on IBM Quantum Platform (https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com/). New users can create a free account and get started today.

items.title: Why Every Enterprise Needs Vision AI Not Just Chatbots | Ft. Co-Founder & CTO, Constems-AI
items.summary: Vision AI is the next frontier of artificial intelligence, the shift that takes AI beyond words and into everything we can see. In this episode of Simulated Reality, Amit Shrivastava, Co-Founder & CTO, Constems-AI, explains why vision AI is the next frontier, and why models built to perceive and interpret images are fundamentally different from the AI we have known so far. He breaks down how his team has spent a decade building vision AI that reads, inspects and understands the physical world. We also get into the AI fear debate: why AI has no intent of its own, what that means for real safety and ethics, and where the regulation conversation gets it right. Plus, what it actually takes to build deep tech in India: sovereign models, productisation, and the discipline of solving on-ground problems instead of chasing research headlines. Amit Shrivastava is CTO and Co-founder of Constems AI, where he leads the engineering and product vision behind the company's vision AI platform, building models that turn real-world images into decisions enterprises can act on. Vision AI is the next frontier of artificial intelligence, the shift that takes AI beyond words and into everything we can see.

In this episode of Simulated Reality, Amit Shrivastava, Co-Founder & CTO, Constems-AI, explains why vision AI is the next frontier, and why models built to perceive and interpret images are fundamentally different from the AI we have known so far. He breaks down how his team has spent a decade building vision AI that reads, inspects and understands the physical world.

We also get into the AI fear debate: why AI has no intent of its own, what that means for real safety and ethics, and where the regulation conversation gets it right. Plus, what it actually takes to build deep tech in India: sovereign models, productisation, and the discipline of solving on-ground problems instead of chasing research headlines.

Amit Shrivastava is CTO and Co-founder of Constems AI, where he leads the engineering and product vision behind the company's vision AI platform, building models that turn real-world images into decisions enterprises can act on.

items.title: Why a Tenured Professor Went Back to School for AI (with John Renne)
items.summary: #realestateai #aipodcast In Episode #1039, Prof. John Renne (Professor of Real Estate and Urban Planning at Tulane University) joins @JonKrohnLearns to describe what happens when a tenured full professor goes back to school for a master’s in AI. John is a world-leading expert on transit-oriented development who spent decades pushing the limits of Excel and SPSS; learning Python and then vibe coding has let him scale that research by orders of magnitude, from 4,500 American train stations to more than 110,000 worldwide. In this episode, he traces how walkable communities went from academic heresy to the most profitable form of real estate development, explains how computer vision can now put a number on how attractive a street is, describes the undergraduate course he and Jon co-teach at Tulane, and makes the case for AI-led oral exams over AI detectors.
